data.name: Vocales básicas
data.description: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ ㅐ ㅔ — las 8 vocales simples

cards.mnemonic: A vertical line with a short stick to the right — looks like a person raising their right arm to say 'Ah!'

examples.n: The silent ㅇ acts as a placeholder before vowels.

cards.mnemonic: Mirror image of ㅏ — the stick points left, like a person leaning back saying 'uh'.
A horizontal line with a small vertical line on top — looks like a little flag pointing up, saying 'Oh!'

examples.n: 소 (cow) is a common animal word.

cards.mnemonic: A horizontal line with a vertical line below — like a cup holding water, 'oo' sound.

cards.translation: Vowel ㅡ — no equivalent; like a deeper 'oo' with unrounded lips (similar to eu in French 'peur')
cards.mnemonic: A single horizontal line — like a flat, neutral mouth. Say 'uh' but with lips spread.
A simple vertical line — like a standing person saying 'ee'.
ㅏ plus an extra line — like a person with a wide open mouth saying 'ae'.

examples.n: 내 (my) is used in informal speech.

cards.mnemonic: ㅓ plus an extra line — like a person with a slightly more closed mouth saying 'e'.

data.name: Consonantes básicas
data.description: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ

cards.translation:
Sound: G as in go (or K at the end of a syllable).
Shape: looks like a gun or a corner.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a gun pointing: 'g' for gun.

examples.t: 국 (guk) – ㄱ at the end sounds like K

cards.translation:
Sound: N as in no.
Shape: looks like a nose or a doorway.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a nose: 'n' for nose.

cards.translation:
Sound: D as in dog (or T at the end).
Shape: looks like a door or a table with legs.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a door: 'd' for door.

cards.translation:
Sound: between R and L (like a tapped R).
Shape: looks like a rat's tail or a staircase.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a rat with a tail: 'r' for rat.

examples.t: 물 (mul) – ㄹ at the end sounds like L

cards.translation:
Sound: M as in mother.
Shape: looks like a mouth or a box.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a closed mouth: 'm' for mouth.

cards.translation:
Sound: B as in boy (or P at the end).
Shape: looks like a bucket or a hat.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a bucket: 'b' for bucket.

examples.t: 밥 (bap) – ㅂ at the end sounds like P

cards.translation:
Sound: S as in sun (but SH before 이).
Shape: looks like a spoon or a hat.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a spoon: 's' for spoon.

cards.translation:
Sound: silent at the beginning of a syllable, NG at the end.
Shape: looks like a zero or a circle.
cards.mnemonic: It's a circle: zero sound at start, like 'ng' at the end.

examples.t: 방 (bang) – ㅇ at the end sounds like NG

cards.translation:
Sound: J as in jam (or CH when unvoiced).
Shape: looks like a chair or a hat with a brim.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a chair: 'j' for chair.

cards.translation:
Sound: H as in hat.
Shape: looks like a hat or a person with arms up.
cards.mnemonic: It looks like a hat: 'h' for hat.

data.name: Aspiradas y tensas
data.description: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ aspiradas · ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ tensas

cards.translation:
Aspirated K — like the K in “Kite” with a strong puff of air.
It’s ㄱ (g/k) + an extra stroke (the puff).
cards.mnemonic: ㄱ with an extra line on top — imagine the extra line is the puff of air escaping.

examples.n: Feel the burst of air on 카.

cards.translation:
Aspirated T — like the T in “Top” with a burst of air.
It’s ㄷ (d/t) + an extra stroke.
cards.mnemonic: ㄷ with an extra line on top — think of the line as the puff of air from a strong T.

examples.n: 타 has a sharp, breathy T.

cards.translation:
Aspirated P — like the P in “Pin” with a strong puff.
It’s ㅂ (b/p) + an extra stroke.
cards.mnemonic: ㅂ with an extra line on top — imagine the line is the puff of air from a strong P.

cards.translation:
Aspirated CH — like the CH in “Cheese” but with a strong puff of air.
It’s ㅈ (j) + an extra stroke.
cards.mnemonic: ㅈ with an extra line on top — the line is the puff of air when you say CH strongly.

examples.n: Same word! Context tells you which.

cards.translation:
Tense KK — throat tightened, no puff, like the K in “sky” (but harder).
It’s ㄱ written twice.
cards.mnemonic: Two ㄱ stacked = double tension. Squeeze your throat like you’re bracing for a punch.

examples.n: 까 is the tense one — tight and short.

cards.translation:
Tense TT — throat tightened, no puff, like the T in “stop” (but harder).
It’s ㄷ written twice.
cards.mnemonic: Two ㄷ stacked = double tension. Tight throat, short and sharp T.

cards.translation:
Tense PP — throat tightened, no puff, like the P in “spy” (but harder).
It’s ㅂ written twice.
cards.mnemonic: Two ㅂ stacked = double tension. Tight throat, no air — like holding your breath.

examples.n: 빠 is tense — short and hard.

cards.translation:
Tense SS — throat tightened, like a hiss with extra force.
It’s ㅅ written twice.
cards.mnemonic: Two ㅅ stacked = double tension. Squeeze your throat and hiss hard.

cards.translation:
Tense JJ — throat tightened, no puff, like the J in “Jazz” but harder and shorter.
It’s ㅈ written twice.
cards.mnemonic: Two ㅈ stacked = double tension. Tight throat, short and sharp J.

examples.n: I drink coffee in the morning.
There’s green onion in the kimchi.

data.name: Bloques silábicos
data.description: Cómo se combinan letras en sílabas completas

cards.translation:
Syllable 가 = consonant ㄱ (g/k) + vowel ㅏ (a).
Combined block: consonant left, vowel right.
cards.mnemonic: The two letters slide together like a puzzle piece — ㄱ is the frame, ㅏ is the vertical beam on the right.

examples.t: 가 is the most common syllable in Korean — it starts many words.
Compare 가 (ga) with 고 (go) — same consonant, different vowel.
examples.n: Vowel changes the sound of the block

cards.translation:
Syllable 나 = consonant ㄴ (n) + vowel ㅏ (a).
Same structure as 가, different first consonant.
cards.mnemonic: ㄴ looks like a nose in profile — say 'na' and touch your nose.

cards.translation:
Syllable 다 = consonant ㄷ (d/t) + vowel ㅏ (a).
All CV blocks follow the same left-right pattern.
cards.mnemonic: ㄷ looks like a door with a handle — 'da' is the first sound of 'door'.

examples.t: Dictionary form of verbs always ends in 다.

cards.translation:
CVC block: 밥 = ㅂ + ㅏ + ㅂ.
The final consonant 받침 sits at the bottom.
cards.mnemonic: The bottom consonant is like a 'cap' (받침) that closes the syllable — rice is 'bap' with a final 'p'.

examples.t: 밥 is the base of Korean meals.

cards.translation:
CVC block: 집 = ㅈ + ㅣ + ㅂ.
Vowel ㅣ is vertical, so the final consonant goes below.
cards.mnemonic: ㅂ at the bottom is like a foundation of the house — 집 means 'house'.

cards.translation:
CVC block: 국 = ㄱ + ㅜ + ㄱ.
Final ㄱ is pronounced lightly as 'k'.
cards.mnemonic: ㄱ at the bottom looks like a spoon resting in the soup bowl — 국 means 'soup'.

cards.translation:
CVC block: 책 = ㅊ + ㅐ + ㄱ.
Compound vowel ㅐ (ae) + final ㄱ.
cards.mnemonic: 책 sounds like 'check' — you check a book for information.

cards.translation:
Compound vowel 와 = ㅗ (o) + ㅏ (a) → 'wa'.
Two vowels combine into one syllable.
cards.mnemonic: ㅗ + ㅏ slide together like a wave (와 = 'come' in Korean) — imagine a wave coming.

cards.translation:
Syllable 봐 = ㅂ + ㅘ (wa).
Compound vowel ㅘ makes 'wa' sound.
cards.mnemonic: 봐 sounds like 'bwa' — imagine saying 'bwa' while looking at something (봐 = look!).

cards.translation:
Syllable 돼 = ㄷ + ㅚ (oe).
Compound vowel ㅚ sounds like 'we/oe'.
cards.mnemonic: 돼 sounds like 'dwae' — think 'do we?' to remember the sound.

cards.translation:
Double 받침: 읽 = ㅇ + ㅣ + ㄹㄱ.
Only the second consonant (ㄱ) is pronounced in most cases.
cards.mnemonic: Two consonants at the bottom — the first one (ㄹ) is silent, like a quiet helper.

cards.translation:
Double 받침: 닭 = ㄷ + ㅏ + ㄹㄱ.
Only ㄱ is pronounced at the end.
cards.mnemonic: 닭 sounds like 'dak' — the ㄹ is silent, like a chicken's quiet cluck.

cards.translation:
Double 받침: 삶 = ㅅ + ㅏ + ㄹㅁ.
Here ㄹ is pronounced, ㅁ is the main final.
cards.mnemonic: 삶 means 'life' — the two bottom consonants work together like life's dual nature.

cards.translation:
Final ㅎ is often silent or makes the next consonant stronger.
Example: 좋다 (jota) → 좋아 (joa).
cards.mnemonic: ㅎ looks like a hat — when it's at the bottom, it 'disappears' like a hat taken off.

cards.translation:
Final ㅇ (ng) links to the next vowel — liaison.
Example: 한국어 → 한구거 (han-gu-geo).
cards.mnemonic: ㅇ is a silent circle — but at the bottom it's 'ng' and connects to the next syllable like a bridge.
